run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:27:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning fired on frontend-proxy's error-span rate, whose reported value (0.0111) matches the magnitude of the frontend-proxy error-span rate seen in the five-minute window ending 00:29Z — a low-level background of 503s — while the alert threshold is 'above 0'. Those pre-alert 503s are Envoy access-log entries with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on GET frontend routes (/api/products/*, /api/data*, /api/recommendations); one traced example at 00:07:22Z contains no frontend service span at all, so the frontend process terminated the connection before answering. Separately, a much larger and clearly application-level burst happened after the alert started: POST /api/checkout returned 500 from about 00:29:24Z to about 00:30:19Z, and in the minute 00:30:00-00:31:00Z every checkout CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span and every checkout->PaymentService/Charge client span was STATUS_CODE_ERROR while the payment service emitted no Charge spans at all and checkout logged repeated [PlaceOrder] lines without its usual 'payment went through'. That burst coincides with the payment Deployment being rollout-restarted at 00:28:12Z (unchanged image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, only the restartedAt annotation changed; new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f, old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 killed 00:28:17Z); the replacement payment container's earliest observed log line is 'Charge request received.' at 00:30:20.991Z, after which charges succeeded again and the service was normal by 00:38-00:40Z. The flagd-config ConfigMap in the same namespace holds two enabled payment fault settings (paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%', paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'on'), and no other object was observed applying a change to payment, so the ConfigMap is the best-supported fault-holder; however I could not read when those values were set, could not observe the declared fault as a continuous condition (payment served charges both before and after the short window), and the pre-alert 503 UC errors that the alert value actually reflects are not explained by it. The conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: At 2026-11-18T00:30:00Z the frontend-proxy service had STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rates of 0.1667/s on span_name 'ingress' and 0.1593/s on span_name 'router frontend egress', against STATUS_CODE_UNSET rates of ~12.5/s on the same span names; these are span counts, not request counts.

The frontend-proxy error-span rate was 0 from 23:25Z to 00:07Z, then non-zero from the 00:09Z sample onward (0.0095/s, 0.0081/s, 0.0111/s at 00:13Z, 0.0037-0.0074/s through 00:27Z), spiked to 0.6/s at the 00:31Z sample, and returned to ~0 from the 00:37Z sample to 00:51Z (sample at 00:51Z = 0).

The frontend-proxy access log contains 503 responses with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET routes: /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM at 00:26:54.748Z, /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z at 00:29:09.832Z, /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars and /api/data/ at 00:31:03Z, /api/data/?contextKeys=accessories at 00:32:46.361Z, and /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z at 00:38:44.761Z.

Trace a72b1518a1c4b0b8d3e417b7c02a95ef (start 2026-11-18T00:07:22.848Z) contains only four spans: load-generator operation 'user_view_cart', load-generator 'GET' with http.status_code 503 and otel.status_code ERROR, frontend-proxy 'ingress' with http.status_code 503 / ERROR, and frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' with tag error="true" and http.status_code 0; there is no span from the frontend service in that trace, so the failing request was not handled by the frontend application.

Between about 2026-11-18T00:29:24Z and 00:30:19Z the frontend-proxy logged POST /api/checkout responses with status 500 ('via_upstream') and 21-byte response bodies, e.g. at 00:29:24.101Z, 00:29:30.223Z, 00:30:00.280Z, 00:30:12.417Z and 00:30:19.401Z.

In the one-minute window 2026-11-18T00:30:00Z-00:31:00Z the checkout service's span 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' had status STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 1.3/s and its client span 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' had STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 1.3/s, while the payment service produced no Charge spans (charge and grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge both 0/s); checkout's own log in that interval shows repeated '[PlaceOrder]' lines without the 'payment went through' line that follows successful charges.

At 00:33:00Z the two-minute error rates had already collapsed (frontend-proxy ingress 0.043/s, router frontend egress 0.0143/s, frontend PlaceOrder 0.0143/s), showing the checkout failure burst was short, and by 00:40:00Z (window 00:38-00:40Z) payment 'charge' and checkout PlaceOrder were STATUS_CODE_UNSET at ~0.88-0.9/s with zero error series.

The payment Deployment carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-18T00:28:12Z; events show ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f 'Created pod: payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t' and Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-79d86bf97f from 0 to 1' at 00:28:12Z, followed by kubelet 'Stopping container payment' on payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 and ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 'Deleted pod' at 00:28:17Z.

Both payment ReplicaSets use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and identical container env (PAYMENT_PORT 8080, FLAGD_HOST flagd, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL_* variables), i.e. the 00:28:12Z rollout changed only the template annotation, and the replacement pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t reports restartCount 0 with no last terminated state.

The replacement payment container's earliest log line in the retained stream is 'Charge request received.' at 2026-11-18T00:30:20.991Z, followed by 'Transaction complete.' entries, then '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 00:30:29.851Z, and from 00:38:24Z onward continuous successful 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo holds demo.flagd.json with, among ENABLED flags, paymentFailure (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', defaultVariant '100%', variants off/10%/25%/50%/75%/90%/100%) and paymentUnreachable (description 'Payment service is unavailable', defaultVariant 'on', variants off/on); all other listed flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) have defaultVariant 'off'.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-f44st was Running and ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-17T23:56:18Z, and its container CPU throttled-period ratio stayed between ~0.23 and ~0.34 of CFS periods across the whole 00:08-00:44Z span (frontend CPU usage a steady ~0.04-0.05 cores).

Sporadic flagd EventStream error spans (STATUS_CODE_ERROR ~0.0037-0.0048/s) are present on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation throughout 00:09-00:51Z, including before the checkout burst, so they are background rather than a change at the burst.

Best-supported candidate root cause: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config holds two switched-on payment fault settings (paymentFailure '100%', paymentUnreachable 'on'); the payment workload whose name they refer to was restarted at 00:28:12Z with an unchanged pod template, and after that restart checkout's PaymentService/Charge client spans all failed while the payment container logged nothing until 00:30:20.991Z, producing frontend /api/checkout 500s and the frontend-proxy 5xx error spans.

The low-level errors that the alert's 0.0111 value actually reflects (00:09-00:27Z) are frontend/Envoy connection-lifecycle resets: Envoy reports UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on frontend GET routes with no frontend application span, consistent with the frontend closing connections before responding rather than an application-level error status; the triggering mechanism is not established by the evidence.

Payment was not continuously failing while the fault flags read as enabled: the old payment pod was serving charge traffic up to 00:29Z (charge span rate 0.611/s in the 00:25-00:30Z window), the new pod logged successful 'Transaction complete.' from 00:30:20.991Z, checkout logged 'payment went through'/'order placed' from 00:30:26.393Z, and by 00:38-00:40Z payment Charge was 0.878/s with zero errors.

The alert fired at 00:27:59Z, before the payment rollout restart at 00:28:12Z and before the checkout 500 burst (~00:29:24-00:30:19Z); the frontend-proxy error rate at that moment was the low-level 503 UC rate (0.0111/s in the 5m window ending 00:29Z), not the later checkout burst (which peaked at 0.6/s in the 5m sample at 00:31Z).

Frontend pod crash, OOM or eviction as the cause is not supported: the frontend pod is Running/ready with restartCount 0, no terminated last state, and the namespace's events in the window contain no OOMKilled, Evicted or Unhealthy event (only the payment rollout Created/Killing/Started/Scheduled/Pulled/ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events).

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate could not be read: list_prometheus_rules (all rules, and rule_name=RequestErrorRate) returned no data views, so the alert's exact expression, window and 'for' duration are unknown.

The frontend container's stdout logs returned no data for the whole window (queries for frontend-675fd7b5c5-f44st returned zero lines with status no_data), so the frontend application's own error text for the 500s and for the failed GET requests is unavailable.
Jaeger returned no frontend traces for 00:26-00:31Z (status no_data), so span-level error details (error message, status code) of the failing PlaceOrder calls are unknown.

A log query for payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t over 00:28:00-00:29:30Z returned no data (status no_data); that empty result only shows the query matched nothing in the retained stream, so whether the new payment container logged anything before 00:30:20.991Z is unknown.

The flagd-config values have no readable change timestamp and secrets/consumer state cannot be read: I could not determine when paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable were set, nor verify that payment actually evaluated them as '100%'/'on' during 00:28-00:30Z; the flagd pod logs returned no data and payment's only flagd-related line is '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 00:30:29.851Z.
What triggered the payment Deployment rollout restart at 00:28:12Z is unknown; only the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation and the controller events are visible.

The cause of the 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} errors that began around 00:08-00:09Z and that the alert value reflects is not established; the frontend's own logs are unavailable and only a handful of such access-log lines were sampled.
Kubernetes events older than 00:12:22Z are not available in the queried range, so the state of the system at ~00:08Z when errors started could not be observed.

A query for NetworkPolicies in namespace otel-demo returned no items, and a query for kube_pod_status_ready / endpoint metric names returned no data; network-level filtering and the readiness/endpoint timeline of payment around 00:28-00:30Z therefore remain unverified.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition (expression, evaluation window, 'for') from the alerting configuration to confirm what the 0.0111 and the 'above 0' threshold measure.

Retrieve frontend application logs (or enable stdout logging for the frontend container) for 00:25-00:35Z to identify why POST /api/checkout returned 500 and why GET routes had connections terminated.

Check flagd configuration change history / git or Helm values for demo.flagd.json to establish when paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable were set to '100%'/'on' and by whom, and whether payment's flagd provider reconnected after the 00:28:12Z restart.
Verify payment readiness probe settings and endpoint propagation around the 00:28:12Z rollout restart to confirm the ~2-minute window in which clients could not reach payment.
Review frontend-proxy Envoy retry/keep-alive settings and the frontend server keep-alive timeouts, since UC connection-termination 503s on GET routes are the signal that actually fired this alert.
